title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 29A (Time limit for arbitral award)

content.overview: Section 29A prescribes the time limit for making the arbitral award, including the period from completion of pleadings, possible extension by consent, and the Court's power to extend the period. It addresses consequences of delay under the current statutory text.
content.glance: Statutory time limit for the award; consent extension; Court may extend; delay consequences as provided.
content.study: Identify the statutory period from completion of pleadings. Parties may extend by consent as provided. The Court may extend on application. Apply the statutory consequences where the award is not made in time.

sections.heading: Time limit
sections.body: Statutory period for making the award from the completion of pleadings as provided.

sections.heading: Consent extension
sections.body: Parties may extend the period by consent within the statutory limits.

sections.heading: Court extension
sections.body: Court may extend the period on application subject to the section.

sections.heading: Consequences of delay
sections.body: Apply the statutory consequences where the award is not made in time.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can the Court extend the time for making an award under section 29A?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Yes. The Court may extend the period on application, subject to the conditions in section 29A.

examTips: Compute the period; note consent and Court extension routes.
